world 2 (key evenhanded).reader_note: "the same number of checks per cart and the same share of warnings that became fines" gives evenhanded outright; "block by block" kills haphazard.

world 3 (key drastic).reader_note: 'towed in nine of every ten cases... a third of vendors had left the trade' gives drastic in one sentence; haphazard is killed by the uniform 9-in-10 pattern.

world 0 (key haphazard).reader_note: "fined on a Tuesday and passed without comment on Friday" and no routes or schedules give haphazard outright.

world 1 (key furtive).reader_note: 'dressed as ordinary customers ... and left without a word' gives furtive directly.

world 1 (key gouged).reader_note: "left a ravine some twenty feet deep along the valley's full length" gives gouged away; "old riverbed lying dry" is a literal hook for emptied.

world 2 (key emptied).reader_note: Census 'twelve families... where there had been ninety' gives emptied; 'leaving nearly every barn and house standing' kills flattened and the slow rise kills gouged.

world 3 (key flattened).reader_note: "every orchard tree and cornstalk lying in the same direction" gives flattened; "soil the water had barely disturbed" kills gouged and the river back in its bed kills dammed.

world 0 (key dammed).reader_note: 'The river behind the jam rose into a lake' states the damming outright.

world 2 (key digressive).reader_note: "moves on to his grandfather's violin, the history of the county road, and a recipe for plum jam" gives digressive away.

world 3 (key florid).reader_note: Easy: 'dressed in the same heaped adjectives and metaphors' defines florid, and the quoted 'molten brass' line does it again; deadpan is directly contradicted.

world 0 (key didactic).reader_note: "closes with several paragraphs telling the reader what the season should teach" gives didactic outright.

world 1 (key deadpan).reader_note: 'in short, plain sentences, and he never remarks on any of them' gives deadpan and kills florid and didactic.

world 3 (key garrison).reader_note: "built barracks beside the town's station to house troops" gives garrison away; dormitory literally fits troops living there.

world 0 (key dormitory).reader_note: 'boarded the 6:40 train every weekday morning and were not seen on its streets again until evening' gives dormitory; getaway is the only near-miss and is weak.

world 1 (key granary).reader_note: "Each autumn the harvest went south by the trainload to the city's mills" gives granary; farm-family population kills dormitory.

world 3 (key honeycombed).reader_note: "went on leafing out and growing as before" kills defoliated, felled and dwarfed in one phrase; the crumbling cores give honeycombed.

world 1 (key dwarfed).reader_note: "knee-high ... while oaks planted at the same time ... had reached twenty feet" gives dwarfed; "spreading and green" kills defoliated/felled.

world 2 (key defoliated).reader_note: 'showed the forest floor through bare crowns' gives defoliated; new leaves each spring kill felled.

world 0 (key handbook).reader_note: "set out, step by step, how to call a meeting" gives handbook; members writing corrections kills gospel.

world 1 (key gospel).reader_note: Gospel needs quoting to settle disputes plus expulsion for questioning one chapter; handbook fits the first half only.

world 2 (key foil).reader_note: Landowner's anti-tenant argument plus demands set against its sentences gives foil; program arranged under its headings makes handbook a strong literal near-miss.

world 3 (key fundraiser).reader_note: 'Few members read past its first pages' kills gospel and handbook; the proceeds sentence gives fundraiser.

world 1 (key dramatized).reader_note: Costumes, loudspeaker narrator, weeks of rehearsal make it a staged show; moving the time for visitors keeps democratized partly alive.

world 2 (key enshrined).reader_note: 'forbade any authority to alter or ban the event' plus the 'living monuments' listing gives enshrined directly; distractors are not near-misses.

world 3 (key harmonized).reader_note: "by the 1980s the processions in all nine villages used the same verses" alone yields harmonized; democratized/dramatized/enshrined are only weakly tempting.

world 0 (key democratized).reader_note: 'opened both roles to anyone who had worked that year's harvest' gives democratized directly.

world 1 (key figurehead).reader_note: Figurehead needs letterhead plus no vote plus administrator-set agenda; 'no vote ever ended in a tie' kills holdout and the administrator kills gatekeeper.

world 2 (key envoy).reader_note: "she traveled to the capital and the county seat to present those requests and returned with the officials' terms" gives envoy outright.

world 3 (key holdout).reader_note: Lone no vote each year under a unanimity rule gives holdout; gatekeeper is defensible since her vote blocked the merger.
